Triage: measurement card on `/meta/*` READ permission-filtering under stub-auth / marketplace-preview boots — auth/permission semantics own the answer → `domain:services` (plugin-auth / security face), type Task, `pm:queue`. The instrument will likely live beside #11373's harness (PR #11472), but the question being answered is an auth-boundary property, and the anchoring rule follows the subject of the fix/answer, not the probe's file.

Grading notes carried from the card, binding on dispatch: measurement first, ⛔ not a redesign of metadata auth; if the measurement exposes an intentional read/write asymmetry contradicted by docs, stop and file for the decision inbox rather than pick. "The two boots are not constructible from the framework harness — here is who can measure them" is a legitimate terminal answer; do not measure the default boot again and report it as coverage. Downstream consumer: objectui#5828 (`pm:blocked`, parked on exactly this half) — when this closes, the unlock scan must re-verify #5828's premise against the recorded reading, and the objectui pin from PR #6103 is the measured baseline either way.

## Round report — both halves answered, **and they answered differently**. Card stays open.

`domain:services` seat (session `session_01APWX2AwT3a4xDcjPCe8bk4`). PR **#11845** is `Part of #11806` and **closes nothing**; reviewed, ready, auto-merge armed. Clause-② **NO** (test-only diff, zero source touched — assessed from the diff by this seat, since the PR body omitted it).

### Half 1 — stub-auth: **measured**

On a boot whose `auth` slot self-declares `{ status: 'stub', handlerReady: false }` with no `security` service:

> `/meta/*` reads are **either refused outright or served unfiltered — never a permission-filtered artifact.**

Anonymous `GET /meta/object/:name` and `GET /meta/types` both answer `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` with the read never running; two **distinct** principals receive **byte-identical** bodies with no mask running at all; `/meta/types` reaches `protocol.getMetaTypes({})` — an argument object carrying **no principal**, so that answer cannot vary by caller on **any** boot.

Two in-repo facts carry it, and both are independent of the auth slot's health — which is what makes the reading a property of the platform rather than of the fixture:

- `shouldDenyAnonymous` (`packages/core/src/security/anonymous-deny.ts`) inspects only the already-resolved execution context — never the auth service or its `handlerReady` — and its `requireAuth` opt-out was retired in **#3963**, so no deployment posture re-opens the door.
- With no `security` service the ADR-0106 metadata-plane mask resolves to `passthrough`, reason `no-service` (D6 tier 1).

⭐ **Consequence for objectui#5828:** on this boot class its benignity claim **holds, and for the reason it states** — the server is not filtering `/meta/*` per user there. So that half closes **measured-shut**, rather than by inference from #11373 (whose write-door reading is a different question on a different boot class and stands unchanged).

### Half 2 — marketplace preview: **not constructible from the framework, and deliberately not faked**

`RuntimeMode`'s `'preview'` member (commented *"bypass auth, simulate admin identity"*) and the whole `KernelContext.previewMode` block are declared in `packages/spec` and **read by nothing**: no runtime branches on `mode === 'preview'`, and `OS_PREVIEW_MODE`'s only consumer widens the better-auth trusted-origin list in `cli/serve.ts`. That boot is produced by the **deployment layer** — `serve.ts` records *"Auth is owned per-project by `ArtifactKernelFactory` in the cloud distribution."*

⇒ Its reading has to be taken in the cloud distribution. ⭐ Refusing to approximate it with a framework test named after a boot the framework cannot build **is the delivery**, not a shortfall — re-measuring the default boot and reporting it as coverage is the exact failure this card was written to prevent.

The surface underneath is filed as **#11846**, which this seat has labelled `domain:spec` / `security` / `finding` (⛔ `pm:queue` withheld — routing is not grading). Note the lane: the declaration lives in `packages/spec`, which **this lane does not own**.

---

## ⭐⭐ The open question that decides how much of #5828 this actually closes — and it cannot be answered from here

The framework reports an **absent** auth slot as `{ enabled: false, status: 'unavailable' }` with the `handlerReady` key **ABSENT — not `false`**. The builder emits `handlerReady` only for a registered occupant that self-declares it, and no framework code ever puts a `handlerReady:false` occupant in the `auth` slot (the only three self-declarers are the cache/job/queue memory fallbacks).

⇒ **The literal `handlerReady: false` on `auth` that #5828 keys on is a shape the framework does not produce.**

| | if objectui keys on… | then |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `status !== 'available'` / `enabled === false` **too** | the stub-auth branch **does** fire on an auth-less framework boot, and this measurement closes #5828's framework half outright |
| **B** | strictly `handlerReady === false` | the branch fires only on a deployment-layer boot that registers such an occupant, and this reading is **adjacent** rather than direct |

⚠️ **`objectstack-ai/objectui` is not in this session's repo scope**, so the implementer marked it **NOT MEASURED rather than guessing** — correctly. It is one cheap grep on the objectui side and unanswerable on this one. **Routing it there rather than leaving it in this thread**, because a question parked on a closed-adjacent card is how a real question goes invisible.

Everything else objectui-side (#5828 / #5746 / #5198 / #5744 / #4042) is likewise recorded NOT MEASURED here.

## Card state

⛔ Not closing on #11845's merge, and the PR is written so it cannot. What remains is the **preview half**, which is not this repo's to measure until #11846 is ruled (or the cloud distribution answers it directly). I am not re-labelling ahead of that merge; once #11845 lands the honest state is `pm:blocked` on **#11846** plus the cross-repo grep above.

## One process note worth carrying beyond this card

The implementer's first `pnpm install` **failed** — `--workspace-concurrency` is not an install flag — and the run still reported **exit code 0**, because the command chain ended in `echo INSTALL_EXIT=$?`: the wrapper's exit was reported, not pnpm's. It was caught only because the next build died on missing `node_modules`.

⭐ Same family as the `cmd | tail; EXIT=$?` trap this board already carries, wearing different clothes: **the last command in the chain decides the reported exit.** Capture the exit into a variable *before* anything else runs on that line, and read the tool's own verdict line rather than a status the shell manufactured after the fact.

Refs: PR #11845 · **#11846** (the preview-mode declaration, filed and routed) · #11373 / PR #11472 (the write-door half, unchanged) · objectui#5828 · objectui PR #6103 (the degenerate-principal pin whose failure this file's control is built against) · #3963 · ADR-0106 D6
